issues.description: Ingest clears warnings/stats but never clears results, so removed input rows remain in the database forever.
Ingest is not atomic; each row is committed independently, so a mid-run crash leaves partial results with inconsistent warnings/stats.
Harness B assumes every JSONL value is an object with object metrics, so arrays, strings, numbers, or non-object metrics crash ingestion.
Non-finite scores such as NaN are accepted by parsing and then crash on insert instead of being warned and skipped.
XML parsing uses ElementTree directly on input files and can crash on malformed XML or be exposed to XML resource-exhaustion attacks.
Missing run_id/model/task values are accepted; empty run IDs collide under the unique key and silently overwrite rows.
Harness A ignores the CSV header entirely, so wrong or reordered columns are silently interpreted as valid data.
Harness B preserves only tags in raw_extra and drops other source fields, reducing auditability of normalized rows.
Epoch parsing guesses milliseconds solely from magnitude, which misclassifies very old or far-future millisecond timestamps.
Invalid JSON and invalid numeric scores are recorded as missing_score, which makes report metrics misleading.
CLI has no error handling, so malformed input or SQLite errors produce raw tracebacks instead of actionable user-facing errors.
Fixture generation recursively deletes the requested directory without guardrails, which is risky for a mistyped path.
Tests cover deterministic fixtures but miss stale-row cleanup, malformed JSONL/XML, empty IDs, NaN scores, and transaction rollback behavior.
